newsitem.title: USA: Moody's may downgrade National Rail Corp.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may downgrade National Rail Corp.

text.p: NEW YORK, Dec 2 - Moody's Investors Service said it has placed the A3 long-term debt rating of Australia's National Rail Corporation (NRC) on review for possible downgrade.
The review is in response to the recent announcement by the Australian Commonwealth government of its intention to sell its equity stake in NRC.

In addition, the decision to place NRC on review was prompted by the uncertainty regarding the future structure of the Australian rail transport industry resulting from the Commonwealth government's decision to sell the Australian National Railways Commission (ANR), the impact upon NRC's operating environment from the uncertainty, and the risks associated with the potential for NRC to acquire or assume some of ANR's operations.

Moody's notes that the original A3 rating was primarily based upon the implicit government support stemming from NRC's 100% government ownership, NRC's importance to Australia's ongoing micro-economic reforms and enhancement to the bondholder of the put option in the event that combined government control falls below 75%.

In addition to the concerns regarding the ultimate structure of the rail transport industry the review will focus upon the impact of any material decline in the level of government ownership and the pressure this could place upon the level of support given NRC's short operating history, the ongoing need for significant subsidies from its shareholders due to the lack of sustained profitable operations, and its exposure to competitive pricing as new entrants enter the interstate rail-freight business.

Moody's notes that the sale of the Commonwealth government's equity stake, prior to the expiration of the shareholders' agreement, requires the consent of all shareholders and the approval of each respective parliament. Given the lack of a concrete timetable for the proposed sale of the Commonwealths' equity stake and the uncertainty about the final process it is unlikely that the review will be concluded in the near-term.
The Commonwealth government currently owns 72.3% of NRC's equity and 45.3% of its voting shares.
The New South Wales government owns 18.6% of NRC's equity and 31.3% or its voting shares whilst the Victorian government owns 8.6% of NRC's equity and 23.4% of the voting shares.

In the event of a sale of the Commonwealth government's equity stake in NRC the bond holders will have the ability to exercise the put option should the combined government control the fall below 75%.
NRC was established in 1991 to operate interstate rail freight business. Previously, Australia's interstate rail freight business had operated on an individual basis, incurring significant losses.
The creation of NRC was in response to the Commonwealth government's micro economic reform process which included improving the operating efficiency in the provision of interstate freight transport.

ANR is the national public-sector rail operator with operations that include passenger services on long-distance routes. ANR is currently losing A$250 million a year. NRC has a significant (approximately 35%) share of Australia's total interstate freight business and is headquartered in Sydney, Australia.
